objective: Convert the typed alias registry into a deterministic, privacy-safe occurrence pipeline that flags lifecycle conflicts without storing private passages.

behaviors: Requires hashes for private source references.
Preserves observed, inferred, proposed, superseded, and unresolved claim states.
Normalizes known aliases while retaining raw values.
Flags conflicting lifecycle states for the same normalized entity.
Produces an order-independent canonical SHA-256 digest.

verification.method: isolated Node.js node:test execution against the exact implementation and test logic before repository write

claims.claim: The canonical queue contains no continuity_mining-owned item.
CM-003's prior next action requested a deterministic alias occurrence scanner.
A machine-enforced privacy and conflict boundary is more durable than another narrative-only continuity artifact.
Future continuity imports should pass through this scanner before publication or graph ingestion.
Private-source continuity can be safely preserved by copying excerpts into repository evidence.
The exact lifecycle of Liminal Thread and General Field Engine remains unresolved until stronger decision evidence is found.

privacy_boundary.included: Alias values, source identifiers, source kinds, source hashes, timestamps, classifications, confidence, lifecycle status, and conflict flags.
privacy_boundary.excluded: Raw private conversation text, excerpts, quotes, health details, relationship details, finances, location narratives, and personal interpretation.
privacy_boundary.enforcement: Forbidden text-bearing fields are rejected; private references require a hash.

limits: The scanner does not discover source material by itself.
Lifecycle conflicts are flagged, not automatically resolved.
No canonical queue file was overwritten because no continuity-owned item is authorized there.
